The whole of [Instruments](elements-instruments.qmd) on one sheet. Every ▶ plays the instrument named. Press **Full screen** to put the sheet on the whole screen for
revision or for the class board.

## The sheet

::::::: {.el-sheet .column-page data-title="Instruments: who is playing, and what they do"}
:::::: {.el-grid}

::::: {.el-card}
#### How many
<p>1 solo · 2 duet · 3 trio · 4 quartet · 5 quintet. A <strong>string quartet</strong>: two violins, viola, cello. A <strong>piano trio</strong>: piano, violin, cello.</p>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Voices
<p>High to low: <strong>soprano</strong>, <strong>alto</strong>, <strong>tenor</strong>, <strong>baritone</strong>, <strong>bass</strong>. <strong>Treble</strong>: a boy's high voice. <strong>Countertenor</strong>: a man in the alto range. An <strong>SATB</strong> choir: soprano, alto, tenor, bass.</p>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Woodwind
<p>Piccolo, flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon. Air across a hole (flute) or through a reed. Top of the score.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-sound="flute" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Flute
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
d B G B|c A F A|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Brass
<p>Trumpet, French horn, trombone, tuba. Lips buzzing into a mouthpiece.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-sound="trumpet" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Trumpet
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
d B G B|c A F A|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Percussion
<p>Timpani, snare drum, cymbals, xylophone, glockenspiel… Struck, shaken or scraped.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-sound="timpani" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Timpani, two notes
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G clef=bass
G, D, G, D,|G,4|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Strings
<p>Violin, viola, cello, double bass. Bowed or plucked. Bottom of the score.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-sound="violin" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Violin
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
d B G B|c A F A|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### The low end
<p>Each family has its bass: bassoon, tuba, timpani, cello and double bass.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-sound="tuba" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Tuba
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G clef=bass
D, B,, G,, B,,|C, A,, F,, A,,|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Band line-ups
<ul>
<li><strong>Rock / pop</strong>: vocals, guitars, bass guitar, drums, keys</li>
<li><strong>Folk</strong>: voice, acoustic guitar, fiddle, banjo</li>
<li><strong>Jazz combo</strong>: rhythm section (piano, bass, drums) + front line (sax, trumpet)</li>
<li><strong>Big band</strong>: sax, trumpet, trombone sections + rhythm section</li></ul>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### What each one does
<ul>
<li><strong>Melody</strong>: the tune</li>
<li><strong>Accompaniment</strong>: chords, rhythm</li>
<li><strong>Countermelody</strong>: a second tune</li>
<li><strong>Bass line</strong>: the lowest part</li>
<li><strong>Solo</strong>: one instrument featured</li></ul>
:::::

::::: {.el-card .el-wide}
#### Check yourself
<div class="eq" data-set="instruments"></div>
:::::

::::::
:::::::

## Describing instruments

- Name the instrument *and* say what it is doing: "the melody is on the **violins**, the **cellos** play a slow bass
  line, the **horns** hold chords".
- More instruments to hear: [Instruments](elements-instruments.qmd) passes one tune round the whole orchestra.

- The longer lesson, with fuller examples: [Elements 4: Instruments](elements-instruments.qmd).
